subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation and helpful context on the invoicing and support use-cases. Quick recap and my recommended next steps below.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary flows: invoice ingestion -> line-item extraction -> summary + question-answering for Ops agents.
- QoR targets: ~95% extraction accuracy on key fields, p95 latency under 350ms for interactive agent flows, budget target <$80 / 1M tokens for inference.
- Compliance: all PII must remain within Acme VPC for POC; SOC 2 evidence will be needed for procurement.

Post-demo recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs summarized):
1) Llama-3 13B (8-bit quantized) — Best balance of quality and latency for structured extraction.
   - Quality: high on extraction and instruction tasks (comparable to larger 70B models on narrow evals).
   - Latency: median per-request latency ~180-250ms on our 1xA100 serving profile.
   - Cost: estimated $35–$50 / 1M tokens (in Dedicated).
   - When to use: default for POC where cost and latency matter and you need strong instruction-following.

2) Mistral-Instruct 7B (int8) — Lower cost, lower latency, good for high-throughput scoring and reranking.
   - Quality: good for synthesis and shorter Q/A; may need prompt engineering for extraction edge cases.
   - Latency: ~120–200ms median.
   - Cost: estimated $12–$20 / 1M tokens.
   - When to use: batch extraction, reranking, or as a fallback to reduce unit cost.

3) Falcon-180B (8-bit / optimized kernels) — Highest quality; heavier on cost and tail latency.
   - Quality: strongest for few-shot summarization and complex reasoning on ambiguous invoices.
   - Latency: p95 can be higher (400–700ms) depending on sequence length; consider batching or async flows.
   - Cost: estimated $120–$180 / 1M tokens.
   - When to use: cases where accuracy absolutely must be maximized (e.g., final QA pass), or for short bursty queries where cost is less of a constraint.

Attachments & links: I attached the post-demo deck and our latency/cost benchmark CSV for these model families. Also shared our prompt set and baseline eval harness in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-benchmarks (see folder "ACME_PROMPT_SET_V1").

Proposed next steps
- If this shortlist looks right, we can:
  1) Spin up a 2-week eval environment in your VPC (read-only access to our control plane + model endpoints) so you can run your prompt set and compare outputs.
  2) Share the eval harness and baseline metrics (we'll run the first pass for you).
  3) Draft a Dedicated quote (Marcus) and SOC2 evidence pack (Jonas) for procurement.

Can you confirm: 1) you'd like the VPC eval; 2) who from your side will run the prompt set (so we can provision eval accounts)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20m tomorrow if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole

Emily —

Great questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) Regression detection + guardrails
- We recommend running automated evals on your prompt set every time you swap quantization or model variants. Our Redwood Optimize harness can run your prompt set and report: accuracy/f1 per field, token-level perplexity, and a qualitative sample delta view.
- Suggested thresholds for POC: reject new variant if field-accuracy drops >2.5% absolute or if top-10 error types change significantly.
- Human-in-the-loop: we can configure a sampling policy (e.g., 5% of outputs auto-flagged for human review) with a priority on low-confidence extractions.

2) Falcon-180B latency for ~400 tokens
- In our Dedicated profile (multi-tenant 8xA100 equivalent), median latency for 400 tokens is ~380ms; p95 typically 520–680ms depending on dynamic batching. To meet your 350ms p95 target we'd suggest either: a) use Llama-3 13B as primary and call Falcon offline for edge cases; or b) commit to a higher-performance serving profile (reserved CPUs/GPU) which reduces p95 to ~300–420ms but increases cost. We can size a quote for both options.

3) Back-of-envelope monthly cost for 12M tokens
- Llama-3 13B (8-bit): ~$420–$600 / month
- Mistral-Instruct 7B: ~$144–$240 / month
- Falcon-180B (8-bit): ~$1,440–$2,160 / month
(Estimates based on typical request mix and our Dedicated unit costs; we'll provide precise numbers in the Dedicated quote.)

Next steps we propose
- I'll provision a VPC eval and invite Tom and Lina (please share their emails).
- Jonas will package the SOC2/pen-test evidence; Marcus will prepare two Dedicated quote options (standard and high-performance).

If that works, can you reply with Tom and Lina's emails and whether you prefer the Falcon-in-async pattern vs larger-serving-profile?

—
Marissa
